question: For a real constant $k$, consider $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=kx+3$. Determine the values of $k$ for which $f$ is one-one. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Equality of function values
Suppose $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$. Then
$$kx_1+3=kx_2+3.$$
Hence,
$$k(x_1-x_2)=0.$$

Non-zero parameter
If $k\ne0$, then $x_1-x_2=0$, so $x_1=x_2$. Thus, $f$ is one-one.

Zero parameter
If $k=0$, then $f(x)=3$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Distinct elements then have the same image, so $f$ is not one-one.

Conclusion
Therefore, $f$ is one-one precisely when
$$k\ne0.$$
